editorial:
The problem here deals with getting the maximum value node from the given input generic tree.

The basic idea here is to traverse the tree and then simply comparing the values to find the maximum for the tree. So to traverse the tree we will use recursion.

So for any node, we will be called recursively for all its children and here we are having our faith that the recursive results would give us the maximum value node from its subtree. So henceforth we only need to compare the recursive results with each other and the node value and then return the final maximum value thus obtained.

Let us take the following example:

Initially we are at root node i.e. node with value 10.

ans = maximum of (10, max(20), max(30), max(40))

ans = maximum of (10, {maximum of (20, max(50), max(60))}, max(30), max(40))

ans = maximum of (10, {maximum of (20, 50, 60)}, max(30), max(40))

ans = maximum of (10, 60, 120, 100)

ans = 120

Hence the maximum value node in the tree is 120.

Below is the implementation in Java:

private static int max(Node node) {
                                    int m = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
                                    for (Node child : node.children) {
                                        int cm = max(child);
                                        m = Math.max(m, cm);
                                    }
                                    m = Math.max(m, node.data);
                                    return m;
                                }

Time Complexity: O(n)

The time complexity for the function is linear as we are traversing every node in the tree to consider its node value

Space Complexity: O(logn)

The space complexity for the function is approximately equal to the height of the tree due to the recursion stack.
